references.text: God's covenant with Abraham, where He promises blessing, which Deuteronomy 8:18 refers back to as the foundation of Israel's prosperity.
God confirms His covenant with Abraham and his descendants, the same covenant mentioned in Deuteronomy 8:18.
God swears by Himself to Abraham, which is the oath to the fathers that Deuteronomy 8:18 refers to.
God's promise to Isaac to fulfill the oath He swore to Abraham, the same covenant mentioned in Deuteronomy 8:18.
God's promise to Jacob of land and blessing, as part of the covenant with the fathers mentioned in Deuteronomy 8:18.
God will keep the covenant He swore to the fathers and bless Israel, a parallel theme with Deuteronomy 8:18.
The land is given because of the promise to the fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, as in Deuteronomy 8:18.
Wealth and honor come from God, and He gives strength to all—the same theme as in Deuteronomy 8:18 that God gives the power to gain wealth.
God gives wealth and possessions, parallel to Deuteronomy 8:18 about God giving the power to acquire prosperity.
Paul writes that our ability comes from God, parallel to Deuteronomy 8:18 about God giving strength to succeed.
I can do all things through Him who strengthens me—the same thought as in Deuteronomy 8:18 that God gives strength.
